storylines.label: DeepSeek Open-sources
storylines.latest_title: DeepSeek Open-Sources dsh-superagent, a Router-Worker Coding Agent

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer on Oct 20, the inference software behind its production models, first framed as a way to cut AI operating costs and then as pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic. Oct 21 coverage added the 155T tokens-a-day serving scale and a high serving margin.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 31–Nov 1: DeepSeek's Harness team open-sourced dsh-superagent, a router-worker coding agent whose architecture is on GitHub, pitched against Claude Code.
editorial.why_it_matters: Two open DeepSeek releases in two weeks, a serving stack and a coding-agent architecture, give platform teams reference designs to benchmark their own inference and agent harness against.
editorial.take_for_builders: Read the DeepInfer and dsh-superagent repos and licenses before borrowing designs; treat the margin and bug-fixing claims as unverified until someone reproduces them outside DeepSeek's stack.

status.detail: DeepInfer is public and unreproduced; dsh-superagent is a prototype with no independent results yet.

storylines.label: Revenue IPO
storylines.latest_title: [AINews] Google admits AI Mode hurts Search revenue; -15% $500B drop worst since 2004 IPO. AI Bear Market coming?

editorial.tldr: On Oct 15 Anthropic told investors quarterly revenue rose nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of its own listing. On Oct 27 Latent Space summarized its S-1, citing 1400% growth and 48% of revenue through cloud partners.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 31: Latent Space ties Google's AI Mode to a 15% (~$500B) Search-parent drop, the worst since its 2004 IPO, as market context for AI listings.
editorial.why_it_matters: An S-1 gives platform teams audited figures on cloud-partner revenue share and growth, which indicate how dependent a vendor is on hyperscaler channels when you plan multi-provider fallbacks.
editorial.take_for_builders: Read the S-1's cloud-partner and compute-commitment sections before locking multi-year Anthropic spend, and keep a fallback provider for any lab whose IPO terms are unsettled.

status.detail: Anthropic's filing is reported public; the Oct 31 item is market context, not IPO news.

storylines.label: Memory Retrieval
storylines.latest_title: Retrieval as Traversal: Value-Indexed Memory for Stateful Long-Context Agents

editorial.tldr: An Oct 17 paper (EPGM) proposed tracking execution provenance so agent memory retrieval stays within a budget. On Oct 23 LangChain described the retrieval techniques its Deep Agents harness uses against clumsy searches, oversized results and stale data.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 29: "Retrieval as Traversal" proposes value-indexed memory so long-context agents stop re-searching for what matters on every forward pass.
editorial.why_it_matters: Agent memory is shifting from bigger stores to cheaper retrieval: provenance, result sizing and indexing decide context cost and staleness.
editorial.take_for_builders: Audit your agent's retrieval for oversized results and stale data, and log which memory entries each answer used; treat the papers as research until code appears.

status.detail: Two arXiv papers and one LangChain engineering post in 12 days; only LangChain's describes a shipped harness.

editorial.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has gathered a Qwen long-horizon agent report, an O-RAN benchmark, agentic-RL training papers, and AWS's SageMaker guide.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 29: two arXiv papers add RL training variants, one rewarding LLM self-learning and one aligning RLVR policy confidence with verifier outcomes (SCARL).
editorial.why_it_matters: Agent RL is now judged on cost and reliability: EnvSched and calibrated budgets (Oct 20) target rollout spend, while MiRL and CalibraRL target named failures. All are paper-reported results, not production evidence; the SageMaker guide remains the only managed-platform recipe.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you train tool-using agents, measure rollout cost per environment (EnvSched, calibrated budgets), log recurring failure modes for error-targeted RL (MiRL), and A/B fine-grained credit against episode-level reward; treat paper results as unreplicated until rerun on your own evals.

status.detail: A loose set of RL items; the newest add self-learning and confidence-aligned RLVR variants to harness co-training and rollout-cost work.

storylines.label: Nemotron 3.5
storylines.latest_title: Accelerate agentic AI with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS

editorial.tldr: vLLM announced day-0 support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Oct 15, covering image, document and video input through OpenAI-compatible serving. OrcaRouter comparisons against Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp followed on Oct 16, and NVIDIA added speech with Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe on Oct 28.
editorial.whats_new: AWS published a guide on Oct 29 for deploying Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model, on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS.
editorial.why_it_matters: Nemotron 3.5 now has a managed-Kubernetes deployment path on AWS alongside vLLM serving, so the decision shifts from whether you can host it to whether self-hosting beats a metered API.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you run multimodal document or video agents on AWS, compare the EKS/HyperPod path with your existing vLLM deployment on your own eval; for voice pipelines, test Transcribe on your own multilingual audio before swapping out your current ASR.

status.detail: Servable on vLLM since launch day; speech added Oct 28 and an AWS EKS/HyperPod deployment guide followed Oct 29.

storylines.label: Kimi K3.1
storylines.latest_title: ZenMux Introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro for Long-Context AI Workflows

editorial.tldr: On Oct 16, coverage framed Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 as a name without a released model, and one report said a new Chinese export-license requirement for large AI models could affect it. Kimi K3.1 Pro launched Oct 24, and Moonshot reset and then restored Pro quotas after user complaints on Oct 26-27.
editorial.whats_new: On Oct 29, ZenMux introduced Kimi K3.1 Pro for long-context workflows, the second third-party host reported after NEAR AI Cloud on Oct 28.
editorial.why_it_matters: Two third-party hosts in two days give a possible route to Kimi K3.1 Pro outside Moonshot's quota-limited API, but pricing, limits and data terms are not in the reports.
editorial.take_for_builders: Rerun your own evals on Kimi K3.1 Pro before routing traffic, keep a fallback model until Moonshot publishes stable quota limits, and compare NEAR's and ZenMux's terms once published before using either as a second route.

status.detail: Moonshot restored Pro quotas after an apology; NEAR AI Cloud and ZenMux now list the model, and a stable quota policy has not been reported.

storylines.label: DeepSeek Flash
storylines.latest_title: Rival.io Launches GraphX, Running DeepSeek V4 Flash on Just Eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash posted AMD MI355X AgentPerf results by Oct 14, and OrcaRouter priced it against rival models on Oct 16. The Flash-1017 update followed Oct 17-19 with stronger coding, cheaper inference and a public search API, and an independent risk paper appeared Oct 26.
editorial.whats_new: Rival.io launched GraphX on Oct 29, claiming to run DeepSeek V4 Flash on just eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs, a self-hosting cost claim the coverage does not yet back with benchmarks.
editorial.why_it_matters: Flash is now cheaper per task, has an independent safety evaluation, and has a vendor claiming a small-GPU serving footprint. Hosting cost and risk posture can both be weighed, though the footprint claim is unverified.
editorial.take_for_builders: Rerun your agent eval and cost-per-task numbers on Flash-1017 before switching, read the Oct 26 risk evaluation before granting tool access, and wait for GraphX throughput data before sizing any L4 deployment.

status.detail: Flash-1017 is out; a safety paper and a low-GPU serving claim are the newest evidence.

storylines.label: Artificial Intelligence
storylines.latest_title: How to Make Artificial Intelligence More Environmentally Sustainable

editorial.tldr: This page groups items by the generic phrase "artificial intelligence", so it is a reading list rather than one thread. Earlier items covered AI oversight bodies; the current window opens with a DeepSeek model upgrade on Oct 19.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 29: InfoQ argues sustainability should be a top-level architectural concern, citing rising electricity use at Microsoft and Google and IT at roughly 2-4% of global emissions.
editorial.why_it_matters: Energy is becoming a design input next to cost and latency; an LLM-search security audit also found weak evidence on /llms.txt effects.
editorial.take_for_builders: Track energy and carbon per workload alongside cost and latency; do not rely on /llms.txt as a security control until isolated evidence exists.

storylines.label: Large Language
storylines.latest_title: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning

editorial.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models", so most of it is a reading list, not one thread. Oct 16-27 items cover sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, steering and continual learning.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 29: Mistral Large 4 is released, with vLLM day-0 support (sparse MLA, speculative decoding, NIXL prefill/decode on Blackwell) and a Hugging Face launch post.
editorial.why_it_matters: Mistral Large 4 is the one item here you can deploy: serving support landed the same day as the weights, so self-hosting is testable now. The papers remain a reading list.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you self-host, pull Mistral Large 4 on the vLLM day-0 build and rerun your own evals and latency tests before swapping it in. Treat the Oct 22 price comparison as unverified until you check provider pricing pages.

storylines.label: Web Search
storylines.latest_title: Cloudflare Introduces Web Search API for AI Applications

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek priced agent web search at $0.75 per 1,000 calls on Oct 17, making search a metered line item. A long-horizon eval paper (Oct 26) and a 4-API community benchmark (Oct 27) followed.
editorial.whats_new: Cloudflare launched a beta Web Search API through AI Gateway, with unified logging, access controls and billing, via REST and Workers.
editorial.why_it_matters: Search is moving into the gateway layer where agent traffic is already logged and billed, so provider choice becomes a gateway config question, but the pricing and benchmark claims are still unverified.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you already route model traffic through a gateway, test its search option against your current API on your own production queries, tracking cost per 1,000 calls and answer quality before switching.

status.detail: A second vendor now offers metered agent search, but sources are thin and the price point and benchmark are not independently confirmed.

storylines.label: Token Efficiency
storylines.latest_title: A Lisp coding agent is beating Codex in token efficiency by 10x

editorial.tldr: Google's Antigravity SDK added local-model support on Oct 14, pitched as a token-efficiency and code-privacy gain. A paper on Oct 23 then targeted the harness itself, where reasoning is re-invoked after tool feedback even when the next action is already fixed.
editorial.whats_new: A Hacker News post on Oct 28 claims a Lisp coding agent beats Codex by 10x on token efficiency; the claim is unverified and the linked source is a social post.
editorial.why_it_matters: Agent token spend is shifting from model choice to harness design: how often the loop re-invokes reasoning and whether work runs locally.
editorial.take_for_builders: Log tokens per completed task in your own harness and test whether skipping a reasoning call after tool output changes success rate before trusting any vendor or social-media multiplier.

status.detail: Three loosely related items; only one is a peer-style method, and the latest 10x claim lacks published methodology in the bundle.
